todo_list.content: Classify the request and complete source intake
todo_list.active_form: Classifying the request and reading required evidence
instructions: Load ceaia-sdlc-story-spec-generation first and only its intake/workflow references. Lock the planned sequence as Story/Test Case/SPEC generation -> independent content review and SPEC status synchronization -> final workspace Story scoring with SPEC metadata -> jira-createissue-helper SDLC gateway. This task owns the four-stage schedule; do not run later stages automatically from inside intake.

This task is end-to-end by default. Set jiraExportRequested=true whether or not the opening request says push/export to Jira, and continue through Jira create/update after content-review PASS, verified SPEC synchronization and final score PASS. Set it false only for an explicit preparation-only/no-Jira request or explicit stop. Do not load jira-createissue-helper, query Jira projects/types, ask for Epic Link, or ask other Jira destination fields during intake; defer all destination resolution until every selected candidate passes generation, independent content review and final scoring.
Classify new_story or existing_ticket_update. A Jira ticket supplied only as evidence is not automatically an update target. Never create a new Jira ticket for an explicit update request.

Before any Jira read, require explicit source WPB, ALM, DATA, FCR or GO independently for every target. Missing source makes the next interaction ask_user_question with one constrained selector per unresolved ticket; no unrelated questions or Jira URL substitute.

Retain the confirmed ticket-to-source mapping. On ticket/source errors show the relevant exact error, ticket and confirmed source; ask correction, same-mapping retry or stop. Never probe other sources.

Inventory every supplied requirement, UX/UI, FSD/API/data, Jira, Confluence and workspace source. For each update read description and AcceptanceCriteria in separate getJiraInfos calls, then complete readJiraAttachments intake before planning or selection. Reuse a completed current-baseline intake; a bounded technical recovery or remote reconciliation may justify a re-read.

Empty/unavailable separate AC is acceptable with a usable description. Record empty-or-unavailable, inspect embedded acceptance statements and continue. Unusable description or incomplete attachment inventory blocks only that target.
Read all returned readable attachments; preserve originals, inventory, IDs and skip reasons. Potentially material unreadable attachments require readable evidence or a supported handling decision.

This is a text-only workflow: never generate or execute scripts, command-line programs or local validation code. Confirm ordinary workspace read/write tools, the scoring tool and an independent read-only reviewer are available. Use observed revisions plus full-content read-back; no local hash or special content-version tool is required. Missing actual file/tool access is a target-specific WAITING_TOOL blocker, not lack of script execution.

Use ask_user_question for unresolved input/recovery choices and yield while waiting. No busy loop, fictional success or automatic stop. UAT-only requests are outside this task: offer the dedicated existing workflow or explicit stop without loading/changing its Test Case rules.

Finish the initial intake pass by recording each selected target as ready-for-planning or explicitly blocked with its exact missing input. Do not silently remove blocked targets. The coordinator may run stage 2 for ready independent targets; a blocked target remains pending and re-enters intake when its input arrives. A missing-source popup still precedes any Jira access.
completion_criteria: Request mode and selected target list are explicit.
Every target's Jira source is confirmed before its first Jira read.
Every update has either completed baseline/AC/attachment intake or a precise recorded target-specific blocker; none is falsely marked ready.
The initial intake pass has classified all targets and recorded runtime/evidence blockers. This stage result is not whole-workflow completion or permission to process a blocked target.

todo_list.content: Plan and generate Stories, tests and SPECs before scoring
todo_list.active_form: Generating evidence-backed Story, Test Case and SPEC artifacts
instructions: Use ceaia-sdlc-story-spec-generation in this task's internal generation-only stage mode. Preserve jiraExportRequested=true for later stages. Read planning, active artifact templates and generation rules; defer scoring-tool-contract and the score call until after independent content review and verified SPEC status. Do not run independent review or Jira writes inside this stage.

Complete source Evidence→SR→candidate mapping, coverage layers, UX inventory, INVEST/decomposition and candidate readiness. Preserve all explicit source obligations; do not optimize for the fewest Stories or invent unsupported scope.

Process only intake-ready targets; finish independent ready candidates even when another target waits. Keep blocked targets selected and pending. This stage cannot fully complete until every selected candidate meets its gates or the user explicitly changes/stops that scope.

Process candidates serially. Resolve current output paths, final SPEC basenames and attachment action before writing Story. Existing updates use source+ticketKey paths and preserve original baseline; distinct selected replacement contents get distinct current SPEC files and explicit mappings.

Write complete STORY.md with exactly one standalone ## Acceptance Criteria heading, stable AC-001 IDs and Given/When/Then in each criterion. Perform read-based parser-shape and source checks without calculating a score.

Generate executable TEST_CASE.md from the supported Story and source evidence before scoring. Preserve the original columns, accurate scenario types, P0/P1/P2 and one negative disposition per AC. Manually inspect every title for standalone or and actual alternative splits. To Confirm is draft-only and blocks final readiness.

Generate primary and any distinctly required update SPECs from active templates. Preserve supplied metadata and approved design references; embed the current Story and executable test table. Existing update attachment mappings remain explicit.

Read back current Story, Test Case and every SPEC once in this stage; check canonical ACs, exact embedding, source coverage, required names and references. Reuse these findings for the generation precheck; do not treat this as independent review or as a score.

A repair may leave stale current files in place but must invalidate their readiness. Supported content defects later found by review or score share the candidate's three-round repair budget; ask immediately for missing facts. Repair only affected files and their dependent embeddings.

Keep outputs/ceaia Story, Test Case and SPEC paths as the latest files and replace them after supported repairs; never create historical deliverable copies. Preserve numbered plans and later score/review records in .ceaia-work while compact state points to current evidence.
completion_criteria: Every selected candidate has current Story, executable Test Case and intended SPECs ready for independent content review; no score is required or claimed in this stage.
Every canonical AC is traceable and executable; no unsupported requirements or silent exclusions remain.
Each candidate has current Story, tests and all intended SPECs; all replacement mappings and supplied metadata are preserved.
Title semantic/lexical validation passes and no stale artifact is declared ready.
No scoring, independent review or Jira write has been duplicated by the generation stage.

todo_list.content: Independently review artifacts, synchronize SPEC status and score final Stories
todo_list.active_form: Reviewing content, then scoring the final Story with SPEC metadata
instructions: Load ceaia-spec-review only now. For each independent content review use a fresh read-only subagent through the platform agent capability; provide actual original sources, active templates, plan, state, Story, tests, every SPEC and update baseline/manifest/attachments. No score response exists yet on a clean first pass. Never replace independent review with generator self-approval.

Reviewer checks STRUCTURE, COVERAGE/INVEST, STORY, TESTS, SPEC and UPDATE. SCORE is DEFERRED until after substantive content review; the reviewer must not invoke scoring, edit artifacts, ask the user or write Jira. Review PASS means content PASS, not final Jira readiness.

Persist every completed review in a monotonically numbered .ceaia-work file such as review-attempt-001.md or the same attempt's post-repair verification record. Never overwrite an earlier review. Keep compact aggregate state pointing to the latest applicable record, plus reviewAttempt and cumulative aiSelfRepairCount counters.

Classify owner and smallest affected file set. SPEC-only problems repair SPEC; test-only problems repair tests and SPEC embedding; only Story content changes require downstream Story/test/SPEC alignment and a fresh independent content review. Missing business facts require immediate focused ask_user_question.

Generation owns all repairs. Score-driven and review-driven content repair share three rounds per candidate/current evidence revision. Each round is one consolidated edit then affected verification; no second edit inside post-repair verification. A failed review or score does not restart the whole task.

After two consecutive no-progress repair verifications or exhaustion of three rounds, stop automatic editing. At most one useful read-only diagnosis may follow. Ask for evidence, correction, environment fix, explicit finite extra rounds, defer or stop. Cosmetic edits never reset budget; substantive new evidence resets only affected candidates with a recorded reason.

Perform one bounded read-based formatting/check cycle before review when needed. Fix platform-owned formatting, names, exact embedding and accidental internal leakage without presenting them as missing business facts. Repeated mechanical failure requires technical diagnosis.

Every finding uses a complete workspace-relative path and actual line when known, evidence, impact and targeted action. Preserve compatibility report fields, sizing decision, source coverage and each SPEC's reviewed binding.

On content-review PASS synchronize only the Result and Reviewer Notes header in every intended SPEC, identify the latest review attempt in Reviewer Notes, then read back each complete file and verify the body is unchanged. Record fileRevision and specHeaderSync=verified; one targeted header-only retry is allowed. The primary SPEC Result and workspace-relative path are the final score metadata. Keep jiraReady=false until final score PASS and global coverage PASS.

After current content-review PASS and verified SPEC synchronization, read the unchanged final STORY.md. Reuse the just-verified complete primary SPEC read-back if no intervening write occurred; otherwise re-read it. Call nodejs-base-mcp.score_requirement_markdown in Workspace mode with relativePath=the current STORY.md, specFileStatus=the primary SPEC Review Result/Result string and specFilePath=that SPEC workspace-relative path. This applies to creates and updates, even when the update ticket key is known: do not send jira_number/source or conversationId to the scorer. Omit force_review/metadata normally. A cache hit may reuse the score while saving this invocation's SPEC metadata.

Extract the single JSON text block; save the full raw response in the next numbered story-quality-score-attempt-<nnn>.md and a short readable diagnostic summary. Record the exact scoring inputs, current Story revision, primary SPEC path/fileRevision and independent review attempt outside the raw JSON. Do not fabricate returned IDs or re-evaluate unchanged content just to seek a higher score. A prior score lacking verified final SPEC metadata is not this final invocation; submit the current metadata once and allow normal cache reuse.

Final score PASS requires a complete current persisted response, boolean ok=true and finite numeric finalScore>=76 within 0–100, with no unresolved AC recognition or parser issue. Compare available acCount and dimensions.sizingSplit.acCount to the actual distinct Story ACs. A low score, parser problem or supported new finding returns to targeted repair; any Story change invalidates its old content review and downstream alignment. An unchanged Story with changed final SPEC metadata needs a metadata-bearing scorer invocation, not force_review.

Set jiraReady for all candidates and updateReady only for valid updates after the current content-review PASS, verified final SPEC status/path, current final score PASS and global source coverage agree. Proceed automatically to Jira preparation. Absence of push/export wording is not a stopping condition. Review PASS alone is insufficient.
completion_criteria: Every selected artifact set and every intended replacement SPEC has a current independent content-review PASS.
Final workspace Story score/parser evidence includes the verified primary SPEC status/path, and source coverage, baseline preservation and mapping agree.
Repair counters and exceptions are compact in state, while numbered score/review/diagnostic records are retained without historical Story/Test Case/SPEC copies.
All headers, final score bindings and upload bindings are current; the original requirement set has no unsupported omissions.

todo_list.content: Prepare and execute the validated Jira operation
todo_list.active_form: Preparing exact Jira payloads and executing the validated export
instructions: Load jira-createissue-helper and enter its dedicated sdlc-gateway.md before any generic create, update or batch route. Set handoffType=ceaia-sdlc-validated only in internal workflow state for routing. Never send handoffType to any Jira MCP tool or include it in dynamicFieldsJson, attachmentsJson or issuesJson. A failed SDLC gate must not fall back to another helper flow.

Validate the actual current final Markdown score record and raw JSON block, its recorded workspace Story input, verified primary SPEC status/path and review binding, latest numbered content-review PASS, verified SPEC-header synchronization, global coverage and every final upload binding. Do not rewrite approved business content inside export; return affected defects to generation and required independent review, then score the final current Story.

Only this validated SDLC stage may read or write user-workspace jira-user-info.md; generic and Test Case helper routes must not use it. Before destination collection, read its CEAIA SDLC Jira Defaults section when present and revalidate saved staffId, almType, project, Story issue type, Epic Link/no-Epic decision and Parent Link. Resolve a real staffId for the required second binding call even if the first Jira call can use JWT identity. On the first SDLC create run without saved defaults, proactively ask for and validate an Epic Link or an explicit no-Epic decision. On every later SDLC run with saved defaults, display the exact revalidated values and require one focused Use these settings/Change settings confirmation before preview. This confirms routing defaults, not final write approval. New Stories include their matching SPEC. Explicit new Epic-plus-Stories requests use the preserved combined branch; never create an Epic implicitly.

Use the live direct tool contracts: queryJiraProjectsByName receives staffId, almType and projectName; queryJiraIssueTypesByProject receives staffId, almType and projectKey; queryJiraCreateMetaFields receives staffId, almType, projectKey and issueType or issueTypeId. Do not use a request wrapper.

Existing updates change only the reviewed non-AC Description, the separately mapped Acceptance Criteria field when its retrieved current value differs, an expressly supported replacement Summary and selected attachment replacements. Description-only/zero-attachment none remains valid when the current AC field is verified to match the reviewed AC. Multiple selected attachments may map to distinct reviewed files in one ticket's attachments.replace array; do not collapse them.

Partition each exact reviewed STORY.md once at its canonical ## Acceptance Criteria section according to the SDLC gateway. Render every other Story section to the Jira Description and only the extracted AC section body to the metadata-confirmed Acceptance Criteria field, preserving wording and order. Convert Markdown presentation to Jira wiki in both fields; never edit STORY.md. Block if AC declarations appear in Description, are missing or duplicated in the AC field, raw Markdown headings remain outside code blocks, or rendering changes meaning.

Show the exact per-target preview, full Jira-wiki rendered non-AC Description and separate Acceptance Criteria field or a verified matching current AC value on update, source-to-field coverage and conversion validation, metadata/links, readable attachment changes and original→replacement mappings. Check decoded effective payloads for each batch item. Exclude standalone TEST_CASE.md, internal score records, planning/state/review files and diagnostics from Jira payloads.

Serialize complete actual first-call exportJiraByDynamicFields arguments once and show them in jira-preview.md. Pass arguments directly without requestJson. For a batch use the exposed issuesJson string, not an unexposed issues parameter. Omit markdownReviewRelativePath from this first Jira create/update call, including every batch item. handoffType is absent from the outer arguments and every serialized value.

No approval tool or final confirmation popup exists for the validated SDLC route. Preserve each numbered jira-export-attempt record in .ceaia-work while jira-preview.md remains the single current preview. Re-read the exact arguments and attachments, repeat final preflight, then call java-base-mcp.exportJiraByDynamicFields immediately with the displayed content.

After each confirmed successful Jira issue write and requested attachment operation, read its actual returned ticketKey; for an update verify it equals the target key. Replace the current jira-preview.md with an exact second-call payload containing only five non-empty direct strings: staffId, almType, issueIdOrKey=that returned ticket key, conversationId=current conversation identity, and markdownReviewRelativePath=the same workspace-relative STORY.md path used in this candidate's final passing workspace score invocation with verified SPEC metadata. Read back that preview and call java-base-mcp.exportJiraByDynamicFields a second time for that item. In a batch, associate each successful item separately using its own returned key and scored Story path; do not send a top-level batch binding path. Keep the first-call preview/result in numbered internal history and record Jira/attachment and markdownReview binding results separately in writeResults.

Execute updates one ticket at a time. At a failed/partial/unknown Jira result pause remaining writes, record known issue-vs-attachment outcomes and reconcile remote state before offering a supported, newly previewed recovery selected by the user. A failed, partial or unknown markdownReview binding preserves the successfully written Jira key/URL but leaves that item incomplete; do not replay the first Jira create/update or successful attachments. Do not blindly retry an uncertain binding. Treat a numeric status=400 as a validation failure even when MCP isError=false. Never replay successful creation or upload to fix only an unfinished step.

After each successful Jira write, update the canonical SDLC-only CEAIA SDLC Jira Defaults section in user-workspace jira-user-info.md with validated non-secret routing values and the Epic Link/no-Epic decision. Do not persist it from any generic or Test Case flow. Failures and partial/unknown outcomes remain resumable waiting states. Ask focused correction/recovery/defer/stop choices; do not spin or declare success. Report each actual returned key/URL, attachment outcome, markdownReview binding outcome and unattempted target separately.
completion_criteria: Every write used an exact final preview/read-back binding for its direct tool arguments and uploaded content, with no approval-tool dependency; first-run create resolved an Epic Link/no-Epic decision and any pre-existing SDLC defaults were revalidated and explicitly confirmed before preview.
No Jira MCP call or serialized payload contains handoffType; multiple SDLC creates use issuesJson when batched, while Task updates execute one ticket at a time.

Every requested issue/attachment operation and its separate five-field markdownReview binding to the final passing Story score with SPEC metadata are confirmed successful, or the user explicitly stopped remaining work.
Partial, unknown, blocked or awaiting-input states are not marked successful workflow completion.
Final result includes individual verified Jira keys/URLs, issue/attachment outcomes and markdownReview binding outcomes.

description: CEAIA SDLC v5: generate Story, Test Case and SPEC; independently review content and synchronize the SPEC Result; score the final workspace Story with specFileStatus/specFilePath before Jira export; then create/update Jira and bind the final scored Story to the returned ticket key using the separate five-field call. Preserve exact previews, raw score evidence and targeted repairs.
